# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall Projector Reports

## Input Quality and Limitations

The complete supplied log covers two reports about the same event A, in room 1 on day 2. Instance identity is clear: two occurrences, one distinct instance. The cause is supported by the technician reproducing the failure, confirming a damaged cable and removing the fault by replacing it.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| “The projector cuts out” reports linked to a damaged cable | 2 | 1 | Both reports concern the same confirmed failure | High confidence in one corroborated incident; insufficient evidence of recurrence across instances |

## Genuine Patterns

None. Two attendees reporting one failure do not establish a repeated problem across distinct instances.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

The identical wording in E1 and E2 could misleadingly suggest two failures. These are two reports of the same event, not evidence of separate incidents or different causes.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

E1 and E2 support one projector failure caused by a damaged cable. The technician’s reproduction and successful cable replacement support that diagnosis. The evidence against calling it a pattern is that only one distinct instance is recorded.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

A person should check the diagnosis and confirm that both reports remain linked to event A. No broader fix or process change is justified by recurrence evidence in this log; the recorded cable replacement already removed this fault.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

This log cannot establish how often projector failures occur, whether damaged cables recur, or whether other rooms or events have similar problems. What recurs here is the report wording, not an independently repeated failure.
